correctness.rationale: Proved for the explicitly specified continuous-time birth–death chains at N>=6, p in (0,1): positivity establishes unique stationary laws, spin reversal gives symmetry, detailed balance supplies exact stationary ratios, and in the upper half a=(k)_3>b=(N-k-1)_3 makes derivatives strictly negative (independence derivative proportional to b−a, anticonformity to 4(b²−a²)). Radial likelihood-ratio comparisons yield strict all-nontrivial-tail inequalities; N=4,5 anticonformity has closed-class obstructions. Exact arithmetic verify.py replayed 24,477 identities and strict comparisons over 400 finite stationary laws; independently solved the N=6 generator. Finite tests support, do not prove, the general theorem.

value.rationale: The central, model-motivated stationary polarization statistic |2K−N| quantifies extremist imbalance. The strict distribution-wide ordering simultaneously settles all high-polarization probabilities, quantiles and increasing loss functions for each finite N and every pair of admissible noise intensities, a substantively stronger risk statement than asymptotic phase thresholds. The N=6 irreducibility boundary prevents interpreting nonunique stationary distributions as comparable on smaller populations.
